title: Small-business protest actions against quarantine restrictions (multi-city episode boundary unresolved)
location: Vilnius (near the Government, then the V. Kudirka monument); Klaipėda City Hall; Panevėžys (Jan 13 Square after participants were prevented from placing wreaths at the Government representative office).
scope: Multi-site social-media call and same-day actions in three named cities; whether these comprise one national episode or distinct local actions is unresolved.
organizer: Živilė Mažeikaitė, founder of ŽM Studija, was named as one organizer of the social-media call; local city organizers and the linkage among gatherings are not fully established.
participants_original: LRT reports about 50 participants joined the Panevėžys action over one hour; Klaipėda had a few protesters and a few supporters; no Vilnius count is reported.
threshold_50_evidence: LRT relays a local reporter estimate of about 50 people joining the Panevėžys action over one hour. The wording does not establish whether this is cumulative arrivals or simultaneous attendance and is not a precise lower bound. It is Panevėžys only; counts from other cities are not pooled. Vilnius turnout is unstated and Klaipėda is described as a few protesters plus a few supporters.

candidate_lead.summary: LRT body confirms symbolic small-business protest actions in Vilnius, Klaipėda and Panevėžys on Friday 5 February, directed at government quarantine policy.

start_date.summary: The page is dated 5 February 2021 and describes the action as taking place Friday; it says the Panevėžys action began at Friday noon.

location_scope.summary: The body names Vilnius near the Government and V. Kudirka monument, Klaipėda City Hall, and Panevėžys, where participants moved to Jan 13 Square after a planned wreath placement was barred.

organizer.summary: LRT names Živilė Mažeikaitė of ŽM Studija as one organizer of a social-media call asking people to gather symbolically; this does not establish the local organizer or common command at each city site.

demands.summary: Participants objected to continued quarantine restrictions, unequal treatment of small businesses and large retailers, and called for small shops and services to reopen with safety measures.

participants.summary: LRT reports about 50 joined the Panevėžys action over one hour; the account does not say whether this is cumulative arrivals or simultaneous attendance. Klaipėda had a few protesters and a few supporters; no Vilnius count is given. No figures are pooled.

state_response.summary: LRT says security staff in Vilnius required distance from the Government building and police in Panevėžys prevented a wreath placement near a government-representative office; participants relocated. These facts do not establish dispersal, arrest, or policy accommodation, so coded dimensions remain unknown.

continuity.summary: This account describes the 5 February actions but gives no exact closing time or link to the 12 January candlelighting in the prior unit.

notes: Body evidence confirms the 5 February gatherings and a specific small-business reopening demand. LRT reports about 50 people joining at Panevėžys over one hour, but does not establish whether this means cumulative arrivals or simultaneous attendance; it is not a precise lower bound. Keep city counts separate and retain pending_unit until the relationship among same-day actions is reviewed. The article mentions meetings with the president and planned prime-minister talks, but does not show a policy concession caused by this action. Do not infer violence, dispersal, or January continuity from silence.
open_questions: Are the three city actions one nationally organized episode or distinct local gatherings under the unit rules?
Does the reported about-50 Panevėžys figure count cumulative arrivals over the hour or simultaneous attendance, and does it support the 50-person threshold?
What was the physical turnout in Vilnius, and can the Klaipėda wording be bounded more precisely?
What were the exact local organizers and the actions’ closing times?
Did a later government decision respond to the protest, and is any causal link documented?
Is any evidence found linking these actions to the January 12 candlelighting?
